security_audit.summary: All 29 static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, JavaScript template literals, or inline file references. Two educational examples remain unsafe: fake password hashing and unescaped HTML interpolation.

remediation.issue: The password example presents a plaintext prefix as a hash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a documented password-hashing library using a unique salt and suitable work factor.

remediation.issue: The tagged template inserts values into HTML without escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Escape untrusted values or return DOM nodes through a safe rendering API.

content.user_title: Modernize JavaScript with Proven ES6+ Patterns
content.value_statement: Legacy JavaScript is difficult to maintain and often hides asynchronous errors. This skill guides refactoring with ES6+, functional patterns, modules, and performance practices.
actual_capabilities: Explains arrow functions, destructuring, spread syntax, template literals, and enhanced object literals.
Guides migrations from callbacks and Promise chains to async and await.
Applies array methods, higher-order functions, composition, pure functions, and immutable updates.
Demonstrates classes, modules, iterators, generators, optional chaining, and nullish coalescing.
Reviews lazy evaluation, memoization, event handling, and other performance techniques.
limitations: Provides general patterns rather than framework-specific architecture.
Does not run, benchmark, or test the resulting JavaScript.
Examples may require changes for browser, Node.js, or build-tool compatibility.
Security-sensitive examples require production libraries and environment-specific review.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Frontend Code
use_cases.description: Replace callbacks, manual loops, and repetitive object handling with readable modern JavaScript.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Patterns
use_cases.description: Create consistent guidance for asynchronous flows, immutable updates, modules, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Learn Modern JavaScript
use_cases.description: Study focused examples covering ES6+ syntax, functional programming, classes, generators, and performance.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Modern Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain [JavaScript feature] with one practical example. Compare it with the older syntax and identify common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this JavaScript function using appropriate ES6+ patterns: [function]. Preserve behavior and explain each meaningful change.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize Async Control Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this callback or Promise workflow with async and await: [code]. Add error handling and preserve concurrency where useful.

prompt_templates.title: Review a JavaScript Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this module for maintainability, immutability, asynchronous correctness, and performance: [module]. Propose prioritized changes with validation steps.

output_examples.input: Explain when to use destructuring in a user profile function.
output_examples.output: Use parameter destructuring when the function reads a known subset of fields. Add defaults for optional fields and avoid deeply nested patterns.

output_examples.input: Modernize a sequential Promise chain that loads independent resources.
output: Identify which requests have no dependency.
Run independent requests together with a Promise coordination method.
Handle failures at the workflow boundary and keep dependent steps sequential.

output_examples.input: Review an array transformation that mutates its source.
output_examples.output: Replace in-place updates with map, filter, or object spread. Confirm that nested values do not require a deeper immutable update.

best_practices: Preserve behavior with tests before refactoring syntax or control flow.
Choose patterns that improve clarity instead of applying every modern feature.
Validate runtime support, error paths, and performance assumptions in the target environment.
anti_patterns: Do not convert dependent asynchronous steps into uncontrolled parallel work.
Do not assume object spread creates deep copies of nested data.
Do not place untrusted values into HTML or dynamic import paths without validation.

faq.question: Does this skill require a specific JavaScript framework?
faq.answer: No. The guidance focuses on language features and patterns that apply across browsers, Node.js, and common frameworks.

faq.question: Can it convert callbacks to async and await?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose conversions while preserving sequencing, concurrency, error handling, and return behavior.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript?
faq.answer: The core patterns often apply, but the skill does not provide detailed type design or TypeScript-specific compiler guidance.

faq.question: Will it test or benchmark my code?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend validation steps, but you must run tests and benchmarks in the target environment.

faq.question: Can it improve JavaScript performance?
faq.answer: It can identify common opportunities such as memoization, lazy evaluation, and concurrency. Measure changes before accepting them.

faq.question: Are all playbook examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. They are concise teaching examples. Security, compatibility, error handling, and operational requirements still need review.
